newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Bakrie shareholders approve stake sale.
newsitem.headline: Bakrie shareholders approve stake sale.

text.p: Indonesia's conglomerate PT Bakrie & Brothers gained shareholders' approval on Wednesday for the proposed sale of its 49-percent stake in PT Indocopper Investama Corporation for $302.65 million.
Bakrie also won shareholders' approval to increase the firm's authorised capital to 1.5 trillion rupiah from 968.7 billion rupiah.
"Apart from gaining approval on the Indocopper sale, the firm has also gained approval to increase its authorised capital," investor relations manager Suresh Kumar told Reuters.

Bakrie announced in late January it had signed a deal to sell its 49-percent stake in Indocopper to PT Nusamba Mineral Industri, a unit of the Nusamba Group controlled by foundations linked to President Suharto.
Indocopper has a 9.36 percent stake in gold and copper mining firm PT Freeport Indonesia. PT Freeport is 81.28-percent owned by the U.S. Freeport McMoRan Copper and Gold Inc.
Bakrie said earlier it would use parts of the net proceeds for repayment of its short-term debts and business expansion.
